items.title: Add audited verification intent repair from existing evidence
items.context: Create a narrow repair command for mid-flight stories whose checklist items lack verificationIntent while passing verificationEvidence already exists. Preserve authored intent and require explicit legacy reason outside PLAN.
items.userSees: A user can run one Lattice command to repair a legacy story instead of hand-editing story metadata.
excludes: Do not make evidence alone pass normal review gates.
Do not rewrite existing authored intent by default.

happy.desc: A PLAN-phase story has passing verificationEvidence refs such as CHK-001:happy:0 but no stored verificationIntent -> lattice verification_intent_repair with mode=fromEvidence dryRun prints reconstructed intent, and the non-dry run writes only the missing lane/index entries plus an audit event; WHY: proves the mid-flight legacy repair path exists without hand-editing story metadata.

edge.desc: A checklist item already has authored verificationIntent on one lane while other evidenced lanes are missing -> repair preserves the authored text and fills only missing entries unless replaceExisting is explicitly requested with a strong reason; WHY: protects the acceptance contract from accidental overwrite.

A DEV/REVIEW/TEST story needs legacy repair -> command rejects missing legacyRepair or a short/empty reason, then succeeds with legacyRepair=true and a substantial reason while recording phase/reason/head/material audit data; WHY: verifies protected-phase mutation stays explicit and auditable.

adversarial.desc: Evidence refs are malformed, point at unknown checklist items or lanes, or represent failing evidence -> repair reports the problematic refs, does not guess generated intent, and leaves checklist intent unchanged; WHY: prevents evidence from becoming a silent or lossy substitute for authored intent.

items.title: Make review and validation diagnostics name the repair path
items.context: When missing verificationIntent has matching evidence refs, story_review and validate should still block but explain that this is a legacy schema repair case and show the repair command.
items.userSees: A blocked reviewer sees a precise next command instead of a generic missing-intent error.
excludes: Do not downgrade blocker severity for normal stories.

happy.desc: story_review sees missing verificationIntent for a lane that already has matching evidence refs -> it still blocks but reports missing_verification_intent_with_evidence details including itemId, lane, evidenceRefs, and a suggested lattice verification_intent_repair command; WHY: gives the reviewer the precise legacy repair path instead of a generic blocker.

lattice validate runs on a story with evidence refs but no stored intent -> validation remains failing/missing coverage but prints the same repair hint instead of implying evidence can pass by itself; WHY: keeps validation aligned with review while preserving intent as the gate contract.

edge.desc: A story lacks verificationIntent and has no matching evidence refs -> diagnostics keep the normal missing_verification_intent behavior without a legacy repair-specific claim; WHY: avoids misleading operators when there is no deterministic reconstruction source.

Existing callers or smoke tests still expect the legacy issue type -> structured output preserves compatibility by retaining the old type or adding a compatible subfield while exposing the richer evidence-aware fields; WHY: prevents diagnostics improvement from breaking current review tooling.

adversarial.desc: Evidence-aware diagnostics are emitted during review or validation -> blocker severity is not downgraded and story_review/validate cannot pass until verificationIntent is actually repaired or authored; WHY: prevents the hint from weakening lifecycle gates for normal stories.

items.title: Use configured gitRoot for INIT_CHECK worktree bootstrap
items.context: Worktree creation must run git operations from the signed workspace material root when metadata root is only a wrapper directory, while preserving existing story metadata semantics.
items.userSees: A valid wrapper-root project with gitRoot can enter INIT_CHECK without manual worktree creation.
excludes: Do not move metadata storage into the nested git repository.

happy.desc: A wrapper metadata root is not a git repository but lattice.config.json has a valid nested gitRoot -> session_brief resolves the signed workspace and story_advance INIT_CHECK creates the story branch and worktree by running git operations from the material git root; WHY: proves valid wrapper-root projects can bootstrap without manual worktree creation.

edge.desc: worktreeDir is configured under the wrapper metadata root while git operations run from the nested material repo -> bootstrap preserves story metadata in the configured store and records story.worktree.path in the existing downstream-compatible format; WHY: verifies metadata root and git material root stay separate without breaking later commands.

Existing non-wrapper projects use the repository root as both metadata and material root -> INIT_CHECK behavior and worktree paths remain compatible with the current single-root flow; WHY: guards against regressions in the common layout while adding gitRoot support.

adversarial.desc: gitRoot is missing, non-git, or disallowed by signed workspace policy -> INIT_CHECK fails with the same signed-workspace reason vocabulary as session_brief and does not leave a partial branch/worktree mutation; WHY: keeps bootstrap failures actionable and avoids split-brain workspace state.

items.title: Cover repair and bootstrap behavior with focused smokes
items.context: Add smoke coverage for evidence-to-intent repair, non-overwrite behavior, malformed refs, protected phase reasons, nested gitRoot bootstrap, invalid gitRoot diagnostics, and the current help-command health check.
items.userSees: The regression suite proves the incident path will not silently return.
excludes: Do not add broad fixture rewrites or unrelated validation framework changes.

happy.desc: The smoke suite creates a legacy story with passing evidence refs and no intent -> it proves story_review blocks with a repair hint, verification_intent_repair dryRun shows generated intent, repair writes missing intent, and story_review no longer reports missing intent for repaired lanes; WHY: covers the core incident path end to end.

The bootstrap smoke creates a temporary wrapper-root project with nested valid gitRoot -> it proves session_brief resolves the signed workspace and INIT_CHECK creates the branch/worktree from the material repo; WHY: covers the gitRoot bootstrap regression in an isolated project.

edge.desc: Smoke data includes existing authored intent plus missing evidenced lanes -> assertions prove repair fills only missing entries and preserves authored text exactly; WHY: locks non-overwrite behavior into regression coverage.

Smoke data exercises DEV/REVIEW/TEST repair attempts without legacyRepair or with too-short reasons, then with a valid reason -> assertions prove protected phase policy and audit fields are enforced; WHY: ensures late repair is deliberate rather than a generic checklist bypass.

A read-only smoke runs lattice checklist_update --help -> it exits zero while no sourceManifestDigest implementation change is required unless the failure reproduces separately; WHY: keeps the excluded P3 regression visible without expanding this story scope.

adversarial.desc: Smoke data includes malformed evidence refs and invalid gitRoot setups -> assertions prove repair and INIT_CHECK fail closed with actionable diagnostics and no partial story/worktree mutation; WHY: exercises failure paths that could otherwise corrupt metadata or git state.

items.title: Sync documented behavior with implementation and built runtime
items.context: Update requirements docs and package build outputs only where the implemented CLI behavior requires it, then verify the global-runtime path can expose the new command after build.
items.userSees: After main is updated and built, global Lattice users can apply the documented repair path consistently.
excludes: Do not expand into unrelated docs navigation cleanup.

happy.desc: Implementation changes add or update the documented repair command, diagnostics, and gitRoot bootstrap behavior in the relevant requirements/story lifecycle docs, then npm --prefix packages/main run build exposes the new command through tracked dist/global-runtime path; WHY: ensures users get the behavior described by the truth source after build.

edge.desc: Only implementation-relevant docs and generated build outputs change -> review confirms no unrelated docs navigation cleanup, broad prose churn, or fixture/story JSON edits were introduced; WHY: keeps this repair story narrow and auditable.

The global or built CLI path is checked after build with the new command help plus lattice checklist_update --help -> both exit zero; WHY: proves the shipped runtime, not only TypeScript sources, exposes the repair path and preserves the excluded P3 health check.

adversarial.desc: sourceManifestDigest help failure is not reproduced during verification -> implementation does not change sourceManifestDigest exports/imports under this story and any reproduced failure is recorded as a separate defect instead of silently expanding scope; WHY: enforces the documented exclusion and prevents scope creep.
